articles.title: Managed RAG search inside the sovereign perimeter: Gemini on GDC enterprise search
articles.text:
National security agencies and other sovereign and highly regulated organizations handle incredibly sensitive data such as classified reports, field manuals, and sensitive multi-modal datasets. Search and multimodal intelligence that’s available in the public cloud can help teams manage and analyze that data, but due to strict data sovereignty mandates, that data cannot leave the customer premises.
The alternative has been to deploy custom agentic search inside a secure, disconnected perimeter, but until now, that meant months building and maintaining custom infrastructure — stitching together models, building speech-to-text and optical character recognition (OCR) pipelines, configuring vector databases, and managing a bespoke user interface.
Today, we're excited to announce enterprise search capabilities with Gemini on Google Distributed Cloud (GDC) air-gapped accelerated by NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra to help solve the above challenges. In preview, this fully managed retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) search experience runs entirely inside your physical security perimeter, with no connection to the public internet or to Google Cloud's global infrastructure. Your teams can now upload their files into a conversation and ask Gemini to find information about it, summarize it, compare it, or translate it. Every answer cites its sources, and conversations persist between sessions.
Enterprise search capabilities on GDC enable your teams to search across siloed data and unlock powerful insights. With these capabilities, you can now:
Go from hundreds of pages to a cited answer: Ask questions across long manuals, reports, and policies, and see exactly which files each answer came from.
Work across languages: Ask in one language and get answers grounded in documents written in another, or have Gemini translate them.
Ask one question across many formats: Combine audio recordings, video clips, images, and spreadsheets with no separate transcription or OCR steps.
Pick up where you left off: Conversations and files persist between sessions, so you don’t have to start from scratch on long-running work.
Keep access need-to-know: Each user's chats and files are private to that user, and access follows the identity provider groups you already manage.
Users can work with PDF, Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files, plus TXT, HTML, PNG and JPEG images, WAV audio, and MP4 video. Each file can be up to 100 MB, and each chat up to 500 MB.
Core architectural layers: under the hood
Let's follow a user query through each layer of the stack: signing in, ingesting files, generating the response with Gemini, and storing the session. Every step happens on the organization's air-gapped network.
Identity and access
Users sign in through their organization's identity provider. Administrators map the service's user role to identity provider groups, and only members of those groups can access the application. Each user's chats and uploaded files are private to that user.
Document ingestion and embedding
When a user uploads a file, it goes straight to the app's object storage bucket. The backend records the file's metadata in the app's managed PostgreSQL database, which is optimized for search. The backend then splits the file into chunks, such as groups of PDF pages or tiles of an image, and writes them to the bucket. A Gemini embedding model running natively within the GDC deployment converts each chunk into a vector, which the backend stores in the app's PostgreSQL database.
When the user asks a question, the state-of-the-art (SOTA) Gemini model running entirely on GDC inside the customer’s data center first rewrites the question with context from the conversation. The backend then embeds the rewritten question with the same model and searches the vector database.
Model serving
The backend then combines the question, the conversation history, and the best-matching data into a single multimodal prompt and sends it to a Gemini endpoint running on NVIDIA HGX B300 systems in that same GDC deployment. Gemini is natively multimodal — it accepts text, images, audio, and video as input, so it can reason across data coming from different file types in a single context, and doesn't require separate speech-to-text and OCR models. The answer then streams back to the user with citations to the source files.
Persistence
Lastly, the persistence layer keeps each conversation's state. Each question and answer is stored in the system’s database and uploaded files stay in object storage, so users can reopen an earlier session and pick up where they left off.
Built for classified and sovereign environments
With Gemini and enterprise search on GDC, prompts, responses, uploaded documents, and embeddings never leave your organization's air-gapped network, and every model runs locally. Data is encrypted at rest with AES-256 disk encryption using locally managed HSM keys, and in transit with TLS using FIPS-approved algorithms. Local IAM integration with granular role-based access control (RBAC) governs access to resources. GDC air-gapped has U.S. DoD IL6 accreditation and is designed to support strict requirements in alignment with FedRAMP High security controls.
Code execution: Compliance and security
To deliver precise, deterministic answers from structured spreadsheet data (such as CSV and XLSX files), Gemini enterprise search leverages the Gemini inference stack's local code-execution engine.
When handling analytical queries — such as computing the average salary across departments — Gemini dynamically generates Python code and runs it securely within Agent Substrate, an open-source execution runtime built for large-scale agent orchestration.
To mitigate security risks inherent to executing LLM-generated code, Agent Substrate enforces strict network isolation and runs workloads inside gVisor sandboxes, helping ensure strong isolation boundaries without sacrificing inference performance.
Bringing frontier models to the sovereign data center
You no longer have to choose between uncompromising security and cutting-edge multimodal intelligence. Enterprise search, Gemini 3.5 Flash and databases optimized for search run together inside the GDC air-gapped perimeter with no dependency on the internet to bring the best autonomous capabilities to the sovereign cloud.
Explore the GDC air-gapped documentation and contact your GDC representative to learn how you can best leverage these search capabilities in your sovereign cloud.

杭州创企连推三款AI母婴硬件，已融资超2亿，拟冲刺港股IPO
articles.text:
智东西
作者 | 江宇
编辑 | 心缘
智东西10月20日报道，今日，AI母婴科技公司两只兔子（Buddy Buzzy）集中发布了3款AI智能硬件：求知3 AI安全座椅、Ori Ring灵犀智能指环和FreeAir AI免手扶吸奶器。三款产品分别瞄准儿童出行、女性健康和哺育场景。
其中，求知3 AI安全座椅搭载儿童专属AI大模型，支持自然语言对话、声音复刻，还能根据环境变化自动调节通风和加热；Ori Ring灵犀智能指环面向女性生理周期、备孕及孕产期健康监测，支持孕期档案管理；FreeAir AI免手扶吸奶器则通过重新设计吸乳结构、增加App智能控制，让妈妈无需一直手扶设备。
此次推出的三款新品，也是两只兔子拓展智能母婴产品线的最新动作。
两只兔子品牌已有约7年历史，最初以儿童安全座椅为核心业务，此后逐步拓展至腰凳、成长椅等品类。其创始人王永拥有约7年的互联网产品从业经验，自2015年起便在儿童安全座椅领域创业。
目前，两只兔子总部位于杭州，产品研发团队主要分布在深圳，约50%的团队成员从事工程技术及产品研发相关工作。
此次，两只兔子还披露了公司的最新经营情况：截至2026年上半年，其GMV同比增长200%，全国入驻门店超过1800家。
融资方面，两只兔子近期完成B+轮融资，累计融资超过2亿元，目前业务规模约3亿元。其计划于今年年底开展C轮融资，2027年业务规模目标约5亿元，并计划在2028年冲刺港交所IPO。
在生产制造方面，两只兔子位于杭州富阳的超级智慧工厂项目总投资约2亿元，目标年产能为50万台。该工厂已完成建设，计划于今年11月启动产线。
一、安全座椅装上儿童AI大模型，能用爸妈的声音讲故事，还能自动温控
三款产品中，AI交互能力更突出的是求知3 AI安全座椅。
求知3 AI安全座椅搭载了面向0至8岁儿童的专属AI大模型，能够通过自然语言与孩子交流。与传统语音控制只能完成固定指令不同，这款安全座椅的AI功能支持开放式对话。
家长可以直接说“兔子兔子，给孩子讲个故事吧”，座椅便会调用AI模型生成相应内容。该产品还加入了声音复刻功能，可以利用父母的声音为孩子讲故事，让孩子在独自坐在后排时也能听到熟悉的声音。
AI还可以回答一些日常问题。如果孩子向AI提出“彩虹是怎么来的”，座椅里的AI能够解释了阳光经过水滴折射、反射产生彩虹的原理。这套AI交互能力支持联网及OTA升级，后续可以持续更新模型能力。
除语音交互外，求知3还将AI引入了一些传统安全座椅的操作环节。例如，AI智能迎宾功能可以感知车门开启，自动旋转座椅，方便家长将孩子抱入座舱。
温控方面，产品能够监测座舱内的环境变化，并自动调节通风或加热，减少家长手动操作的频率。
不过，对于安全座椅来说，基础的安全防护仍然是核心。求知3 AI安全座椅获得德国E1 i-Size认证及中国3C认证，并配备智能侧面防护结构。当车辆遭遇侧向碰撞时，相关侧防装置可以通过弹出结构辅助缓冲冲击。
另一项功能是儿童遗忘报警。求知3 AI安全座椅提供车内灯显、App通知和人工电话三重提醒机制，尝试降低孩子被遗忘在车内的风险。
舒适性方面，这款安全座椅支持最大170°躺角、8档调节，覆盖身高40cm至150cm的儿童，并配备可拆卸睡垫以及座舱、睡垫双通风设计。
二、一枚6.1毫米智能戒指，关注女性从备孕到产后的身体变化
第二款产品Ori Ring灵犀智能指环，将AI应用到了女性健康监测场景。
两只兔子此次推出的Ori Ring，围绕月经周期、备孕、怀孕和产后这些阶段提供连续的数据记录和分析。
Ori Ring采用6.1mm纤窄环身设计，通过微型传感器采集身体数据，结合算法提供女性生理周期及易孕窗口参考。
在日常使用中，这款戒指能够监测睡眠、心率、压力等指标，并记录月经周期相关变化。
现场产品负责人介绍，女性在不同生理周期内，体温、睡眠等数据可能出现细微波动。通过硬件持续采集数据，再结合算法进行分析，Ori Ring可以为使用者提供生理周期预测。
进入备孕阶段后，该系统能够结合长期身体数据，提供排卵期提示和易孕窗口参考。
而到了孕期，这款产品的功能更丰富。例如，孕早期可以查看孕周、预产期等信息；孕中期可以归档产检报告，记录胎动等情况；孕晚期则支持宫缩记录、预产期倒计时及运动建议。产后，系统还可以持续跟踪身体变化，提供恢复相关建议。
现场介绍中，两只兔子还提到了利用AI辅助理解孕期检查数据的思路。
对于孕妈妈来说，多次产检产生的报告往往包含不同指标。如果能将这些信息与日常睡眠、生理变化记录结合，便可以更方便地回顾身体状态，并在就医时向医生提供参考。
不过，这些数据与AI生成的分析结果仍属于辅助健康管理信息，不能替代专业医学检查和诊断。
硬件设计方面，Ori Ring也针对女性长期佩戴的需求做了一些调整。
戒指采用低致敏不锈钢材质，提供银色、玫瑰金等配色，单指环续航约7天，并支持50米防水。考虑到部分女性在孕期可能出现手指水肿、原有戒指尺寸不再合适的情况，两只兔子还推出了Care+孕期换圈服务。
另一项设计是离线记录。用户可以主动关闭戒指的无线通信功能，让数据暂时保存在设备中，之后再进行同步。在不需要实时连接手机时，用户仍可以连续记录一段时间的身体数据。
三、吸奶器缩至241克：无线免手扶，还能用App遥控
第三款产品FreeAir AI免手扶吸奶器，解决的是妈妈长时间扶住设备的问题。FreeAir将泵机与集乳杯做成一体化结构，不需要外接长管，可以直接放入内衣中使用。
其单边重量为241克，最大工作档位噪声约53分贝，配件数量精简至4件。两只兔子参考了一项涵盖605例中国女性的乳房形态测量研究，对传统吸奶器喇叭罩的尺寸和内部曲线进行了重新设计。
具体来看，FreeAir将乳汁通道深度调整至16.01mm，较其参考的欧美均码设计缩短约25%，并采用三段式内壁曲线，改善贴合度。考虑到不同使用者的身体差异，该产品除了24mm喇叭罩，还提供17mm、19mm和21mm三种尺寸的硅胶内塞。
吸乳方式方面，FreeAir采用仿生微震脉冲设计，尝试模拟婴儿吮吸时的节奏变化。产品最大吸力达到280mmHg，提供刺激、按摩、吸乳及自动四种模式。
其中，刺激模式采用短而快的吸力节奏；吸乳模式则采用相对长而慢的节奏；自动模式可以在刺激和吸乳之间进行切换，降低新手使用者的操作难度。各模式还支持多档位调节，用户可以根据自己的舒适程度选择适合的参数。
此次，FreeAir也加入了App智能控制功能。用户可以通过手机远程启停设备、调节吸力档位以及切换吸乳模式。例如，在夜间或双手不方便操作时，可以直接在App中修改设备设置，无需反复摸索机身按键。
记录方面，系统可以保存吸奶时长、模式等使用数据，用户还可以手动录入每次吸出的奶量，生成阶段性的喂养记录和趋势信息。
该产品同时支持个性化模式记忆。用户设置好适合自己的吸力档位和节奏后，下次使用时可以直接调用，无需重新调整。
结语：AI母婴硬件，还要过长期使用这一关
纵观此次三款AI硬件，一个值得关注的变化是，AI正在进入过去较少受到科技行业关注的细分生活场景。这些场景对产品的安全、舒适、稳定性和使用便利性提出了很高要求。
对母婴硬件来说，让家长愿意每天使用、放心长期使用，才是AI真正进入育儿生活需要解决的问题。

articles.title: Translating in style: An open-weight alternative to GPT-4 for culturally aligned machine translation
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.23868v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Machine translation systems often preserve meaning but systematically flatten linguistic style, a failure that is most acute when translating into non-Western languages. The RASTA framework of Havaldar et al. (2025a) addresses this through retrieval-augmented stylistic alignment, but relies on GPT-4, a closed, proprietary model. We investigate whether an open-weight translation specialist, Hunyuan-MT-7B, can serve as an open-weight alternative. We evaluate three variants of the model, the base model, a LoRA supervised fine-tune, and a GRPO-steered policy. We do this across three style dimensions (formality, politeness, and intimacy) and twelve directed language pairs, measuring style alignment with the correlation-based metric $\mathcal{A}$. We find that fine-tuning does not reliably improve alignment: the three variants are statistically indistinguishable in aggregate. The open backbone does not match RASTA-GPT-4 overall, but the shortfall is concentrated in formality and largely closes for intimacy and Chinese directions, where the open model matches or surpasses GPT-4 on individual pairs. An accessible RASTA pipeline built on an open model is thus already viable for parts of the problem.

articles.title: https://www.anthropic.com/research/a-postmortem-of-three-recent-issues
Write Once, Check Many: Reusable Ledgers for Post-Hoc Policy Compliance Auditing of Agent Trajectories
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.24483v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Auditing LLM agents against policies is critical to ensure safety but requires rereading long trajectories once per policy. Can we instead record each trajectory once and reuse that record for policies not known in advance? We propose write once, check many, a framework in which a writer model converts each agent trajectory into a policy-independent ledger of the agent's actions and outcomes. A reader then checks each new policy against the ledger alone, without access to the original trajectory. On 900 trajectories from SHADE-Arena, $\tau$-bench, and $\tau^2$-bench, we show that a 12B reader of narrative ledgers can either match or in fact achieve higher AUC than the same 12B model reading full trajectories. On SHADE-Arena policies that combine several facts, our approach outperforms a 31B model reading the trajectory (.777 vs. .713 AUC). When checking eight SHADE-Arena policies separately, ledgers use about $5\times$ fewer tokens, including the cost of writing them. A deeper analysis shows that rule-based extraction performs better on some single-action policies, and ledgers can miss evidence in long tool outputs and message contents. Our results suggest that reusable, policy-independent records can make retrospective agent auditing more efficient and effective, and highlight important considerations in ledger design.

articles.title: SpaceX’s Musk Lauds Its Soaring Cloud Business and Possible Tesla Merger
articles.text:
SpaceX put on a bit of a show for shareholders today—and I’m not referring to the sizzle reel of rocket and space videos it showed on its earnings call. No, the big attention grabber was the update from CEO Elon Musk on the progress of SpaceX’s contemplated merger with Tesla and just how involved—or not involved he is in the whole affair.
First though, it’s worth mentioning the other big highlight from the call: SpaceX’s booming AI—excuse me, SI—business, a category that includes the company’s X social media service, its Grok Bot agent platform and a cloud infrastructure service it has started to rent to outsiders like Anthropic. The segment is on fire. It saw its third-quarter revenue nearly triple to $7.56 billion, making it the largest business category at SpaceX. And if that wasn’t enough, the SI business swung to an operating profit of $431 million from a $1.26 billion loss in the second quarter.
SpaceX shares jumped nearly 7% in after-hours trading following the report.
SpaceX executives made it clear that the big story in its SI (superintelligence) segment is its cloud business. Musk told investors the company’s phone is ringing off the hook with demand from businesses that want to lease SpaceX’s AI compute. “We are hounded relentlessly by every hyperscaler and by dozens of smaller companies to rent more of our compute,” Musk said. “We could rent out our compute several times over if we said yes to everyone.”
For his part, Bret Johnsen, SpaceX’s chief financial officer, described that demand as “extraordinary” and said at the prices it’s currently charging its cloud customers, SpaceX is “generating a payback in less than a year” on new data centers after it deploys them.
Musk also addressed a question from an investor about his desire to unite SpaceX and Tesla. He said the respective companies have formed special committees to examine a merger, but because he’s CEO of both Tesla and SpaceX, he has needed to recuse himself from those discussions.
Still, that didn’t stop him from telling everyone listening to the call that he thinks a merger is a grand idea. “I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining both companies,” he said.
Musk also stated the obvious caveat: Any deal will still need shareholder approval, and there’s no guarantee they’ll bless it. “I think some people assume a SpaceX-Telsa merger is a certainty,” he said. “I think that would be overstating it.” Nonetheless, Musk’s shareholders tend to be very obedient to him. If the companies decide to move forward with a merger, stay tuned for Musk to start turning up his X megaphone and encouraging them to fall in line.
Netflix’s Sad Trombone
The other shoe just dropped at Netflix. Last than a week after announcing the layoffs of about 1,000 employees, or 6% of the company, Netflix reported its weakest quarterly revenue growth in three years—an 11.8% jump to $12.87 billion in revenue. For a figure lower than that, you have to go all the way back to the third quarter of 2023. It didn’t help that Netflix told investors revenue growth will get even worse in the fourth quarter, estimating 11.5% for that period. The company’s shares fell 5% in after-hours trading.
The weak third-quarter revenue number wasn’t exactly a surprise; it was slightly better than the growth rate Netflix had told analysts to expect last quarter. But it’s obvious from the heads that have rolled at Netflix over the past week that the company’s CEOs, Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters, aren’t happy with the state of its business. The firings included Bela Bajaria, chief content officer, and David Lin, film chief, a sign that the company wants to reset its approach to movies and series. It's still a powerhouse in living rooms: The new season of “The Diplomat” is back on with a vengeance on my TV set. But Netflix feels like it’s looking for a new act.
In Other News
In a draft IPO prospectus, Anthropic disclosed a net loss of more than $80 billion for the first half of the year, reflecting its accounting for financing agreements, The Wall Street Journal reported. Around a fifth of its $16.3 billion in revenue for the period came from two customers.

articles.title: AI来抢百度网页搜索市场了：DeepSeek最便宜还没广告
articles.text:
快科技10月20日消息，PC时代互联网搜索引擎市场谷歌全球称霸，国内则是百度独大，现在是AI时代了，网页搜索这个市场也多了很多选择，DeepSeek、腾讯、阿里等都有搜索API服务。
前几天DeepSeek发布V4.1 Flash-1017版大模型的时候，宣布了一个新的服务——首次向开发者开放自研搜索引擎的Search和Fetch API，开发者可以让Agent直接搜索网页、抓取正文。
两个接口均按成功请求计费，每千次5元，不过这是搜索成功之后的价格，请求失败、搜索无结果或超时不计费。
通过 Claude Code、Codex 内置网页搜索功能触发的Search请求，前两周暂免接口调用费。
官方介绍称，DeepSee搜索是AI原生的通用搜索引擎，索引了全球千亿级网页，支持多语言搜索，实时返回高相关、高权威、高时效的优质结果。
针对SEO作弊、GEO操纵和低质AIGC，DeepSeek通过严格的识别机制进行过滤，确保向用户与LLM呈现权威可信的信息。
从这些信息可以看出，DeepSeek的搜索不仅价格便宜，而且屏蔽了劣质结果，尤其是让人痛恶的SEO、GEO等人为操作的垃圾结果，用过搜索的网友都知道这个的含金量。
DeepSeek的搜索API本质上是服务Agent的，并不是单独的网页，但这也不是难事，知乎上已经有网友让AI写了个程序，直接当搜索引擎用了，还对比了百度的搜索结果，孰优孰劣一目了然，DeepSeek现在是没有广告和竞价排名的。
除了DeepSeek之外，腾讯日前也开放了他们的搜索API服务元宝搜索，也是千亿级索引，日均调用数亿次，已经支撑 WorkBuddy、ima、腾讯视频等 50 多项内部业务。
不过元宝搜索的价格比DeepSeek高得多，速版、标准版和旗舰版每千次调用分别收费14 元、20元和26元，另外提供每月2000次免费额度。
此外，极速版仅支持公开网页信源，要使用权威垂直信源，至少需要选择20元的标准版。
更早之前，阿里、智谱、字节火山等公司也早推出了搜索API业务，还有大量第三方的搜索API，比如exa、anysearch、博查等。
这些搜索API服务中，目前DeepSeek的费用是最低的，不过其他提供收费服务的公司往往也有免费额度，普通人日常搜索是够用的，需要高频率或者专业搜索结果的可以考虑付费。
有了这些服务，不仅可以在Agent中使用，有需要的网友完全可以用它们来打造一个属于自己的搜索引擎，直接让AI去写个程序就可以了，可以享受到无广告和SEO/GEO的搜索质量。

articles.title: Meta Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations
articles.text:
Muse, the new general-purpose AI agent from Meta, can expose sensitive information when users share conversations through web links, researchers reported Monday. In response to questions from Ars about the behavior, Meta said it's suspending the sharing feature while the company reviews it and considers making changes.
Like many online services, Muse has allowed users to share searches, conversations, images, and similar content with other people. Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. To keep potentially sensitive information from being accessible to unintended people, the URLs typically contain a long sequence of text that can’t be easily guessed.
A single query is all that's required
Muse, which Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said last month was “built from the ground up for privacy and security,” seems to take the same precautions. But a central design decision for constructing URLs has made the links easy to discover. As a result, researchers from security firm Claroc said they were able to enumerate 6,800 links Muse users created for sharing conversations with others. After opening a few hundred of them, the researchers found information that was clearly not intended to be publicly available, including:

articles.title: 比亚迪也能用Carplay了？这老哥造福了无数新能源车主
articles.text:
被车企抛弃的老车主们，这回能免费用上 Carplay 了。
就在去年，咱们跟差友讲过同事小曲去年的故事。（才买2年就被车企“抛弃”？这群车主开始破解车机了。）
虽然新能源车带着整个车市越来越智能，但这些老车主们却好像被战略牺牲了。
应用少、更新慢、功能落后，时代红利一口没吃上，反而被拍死在了沙滩上。
没办法，小曲只能破解车机白名单+外装一个盒子，在老款零跑 C01 用上了Carplay。
其实也不只是小曲这些 “老旧新能源车”，燃油车也是一样。
那些处于半新不新的 “智能车机”，跟界面清新的 Carplay 比起来，和砖头没啥区别。
8 代凯美瑞
可就在前几天，一个叫 DiPlay 的 app 火了起来，一瞬间超过了小曲数年的努力。
视频平台上关于 DiPlay 的，随便一条都是上千点赞。
这玩意是一款针对比亚迪老车机的 Carplay 破解软件，在 Github 上免费开源，且操作极其简单。
人家就是一个 app，安装就完事了，都不用打开 ADB（安卓调试桥）。
开发者 Shihub 还贴心的做了一个网站，下载按钮直接怼你脸上。
甚至甚至，你登不上 Github，也看不懂英文，一些视频博主还会教你通过豆包下载，纯纯的傻瓜式操作。
不过哈，简单好用只是第一步，DiPlay 的泛用性才是出圈的真正原因。
如果大伙有印象的话，比亚迪以前的 Dilink 车机都是基于安卓开发的。
然后不知道哪位老哥鬼脑发动，把 DiPlay 用在了其他安卓设备上。
这下不仅是比亚迪，吉利、长安、林肯、丰田。。。只要能装安装包的机子，基本都能用 DiPlay。
这下 DiPlay 真成 “源神” 了。
那么，这玩意用起来如何呢？我觉得有点看脸。
我们拿来两台同事的车，一台是 23 款的元 Plus，一台是 21 款的宋 Plus，Dilink 版本都是 3.0。
先说失败的元 Plus 吧。
安装方面没问题，比亚迪老车型对安装包没有限制，提前下好放在 U 盘里，一插进去就能识别出来。
手机与车机的连接 Diplay 里面也有操作指示，按部就班操作就行。
可最后就卡在了 Carplay 激活那一步，明明手机已经弹出了 Carplay 的窗口，但车机一直在搜索，始终无法连接。
咱们换了 4 个不同版本的 apk，始终无法安装。最后在一个 DiPlay 互助群里，看到群主说这种情况应该就是车型无法适配，莫得办法了。
而另一边的宋 Plus 就顺利得多咯，一次就成功，用起来挺流畅。
不得不说，看着这个 UI 再对比一下比亚迪的原车机，真挺舒服的。
具体的功能就没啥好说了，导航可以顺利从手机流转到车机上，也能实现车道级导航。
网易云也可以直接让 Siri 打开日推。
甚至切歌会卡这个跟 Carplay 盒子那种方案也是一样的。。。
可是，在一些与原车结合的功能上，问题就出来了。
比如说比亚迪语音助手 “小迪”，它的默认优先级比 Siri 更高，同时呼出的时候，Siri 就静默了。
这里咱们试了一下，当我说打开网易云的时候，小迪依旧在聆听，优先级更高的它，直接帮我打开了车机的网易云，即使我喊的 Siri 也没用。
而在音量的调节上，高德地图和网易云用的是同一个频道，音量只能一起调大调小。
如果咱们再扣细一点的话，听音乐的音频也有问题。
停着的时候没啥事，但当车辆在行驶的时候，音乐的延迟会导致时不时歌曲会自动加速，和抢拍了一样。
在视频的第18秒，音乐突然加速了一下。
要打电话就更蛋疼了，我们先测的微信电话，当外面的电话打进来的时候，车机界面并没有通话的弹窗，需要进应用里面自己点击。
正常的电话更加离谱，根本听不清对方在说什么。
为了避免是信号干扰，我们同样的手机和地点，用比亚迪的车机再试了一次，其实就是 Diplay 拉了。
如果大伙真想打电话，其实原本的车机就没啥不好的，功能嘛，怎么方便怎么来。
所以，Diplay 在车机上能干的活很明显了，就是导航跟听歌，一如原生 Carplay 那样干净。
毕竟本身 Carplay 好看之外，也是解放你的 iPhone，没必要拿个手机支架挂在那里而已。
后来咱们还找了 17 款宋、22 款宋，25 款长安启源 A06、22 款驱逐舰 05 四位车友，让他们也试了一下。
结果还行，其中前三位都成功了，只有驱逐舰 05 没成功装上。
不过在成功的几位里面也有差异，启源的哥们说他觉得依旧有点卡，不如自己的原生车机。
宋车友则是装了一个新出的飞屏版安装包，连导航都投到了仪表盘上（以前的比亚迪仪表盘没有地图导航显示）。
但也有可能只是 DiPlay 对宋这个车型支持做的比较好，换作是其他车，依旧有着各种各样的问题。
比如 CarPlay 是有的，但音乐没法走车机音频通道，还是手机在播放。
或者是音乐没毛病，但语音电话的时候对方没声音。
总之，DiPlay 还是会受到车型、网络、安卓版本等东西的影响。真要彻底弄清楚，还是得端个电脑到车上把 log（系统日志）抓出来才行。
同样有不少车主出现连接不上的问题。
不过开源已经够伟大了，要求也不能太高，人家可是免费给你用诶。
而且作者老哥到现在还在 GitHub 上不断回复网友的问题，这个项目到现在收藏量已经达到 1.15w，有着 228 个未解决的提问，真忙炸了。
对于一个程序员专用的小众平台来说，挺夸张的了。
当然，动手能力强的哥们肯定会乐在其中。
刚写到这的时候，脖子哥看到有人魔改了 DiPlay，给 Mac 也装上了 Carplay。
还能这么玩。
你要是着实喜欢 Carplay 的界面，那么你家的电视也不是不可以。
也有豪气冲天的摩友直接拿手机装个 Diplay 用 Carplay（不是哥们，你兜里不就揣着一部苹果手机吗？直接导航不行吗？）
还有整个萤火虫车机破解，然后把 DiPlay 装进去的。。。
目前帖子已经没了，大伙不要模仿，会影响质保的。
但假如你只是想简单在车机上用一用 Carplay，只能祈祷自己一次安装成功咯，不然就回到最开始那种要么花钱要么折腾的循环中了。
不过哈，我觉得这玩意现在火成这样应该活不了太久。
因为 DiPlay 这断的是果子的财路。
Carplay 本身是一个闭源的投屏协议，苹果为了保护生态安全和商业利益，推行了一个叫 MFi（Made for iPhone）的认证体系。
简单来讲，每一个想跟 iPhone 建立 Carplay 连接的设备，都必须用上一颗苹果的加密芯片，里面包含了私钥和身份信息，不然就连不上。
虽然从来都没有具体的数据证明苹果向车企收了多少钱，但车企们肯定不爽的。
比如宝马就试过搞 Carplay 订阅制，80 美元一年。虽然很快就被喷没了，但也能表明他们的一个态度。
而一年卖几百万辆的比亚迪，也就直到今年 9 月，才第一次用上 Carplay。
甚至直到现在，还有大量的车型依旧没有配 Carplay。
而外面一个 Carplay 盒子也要 2、300 块，这也是免费开源的 DiPlay 能引起轩然大波的原因。
那 Shihub 是怎么做的呢？
哥们买了一个市面上已经通过了 MFi 认证的正版 Carplay 硬件，然后通过抓包等技术手段，把这颗芯片的私钥给提取了出来，放在了 DiPlay 的安装包里。
那么当 iPhone 和 DiPlay 连接的时候，在 iPhone 眼里 DiPlay 就是一个正版软件，顺利通过了认证。
这种做法其实也不少见，以前某些盗版 Carplay 盒子也是这么干的。
但是，DiPlay 这波开源，结合差评君前几天写的那个大逆向的事，一下人人都能用上免费 Carplay，传播的力度可就大大不一样了。
那换做你是果子，这你能忍？
所以，如果苹果再不革新一下自己的 MFi 认证，不然接下来估计我们能看到更多千奇百怪的 Carplay 了。

articles.title: Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.24236v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but often reduces the diversity of their reasoning behaviors. We study this phenomenon from the perspective of finite-sample learning dynamics and show that limited on-policy rollouts can progressively suppress semantically distinct but equally rewarded reasoning modes. Once a mode becomes sufficiently under-sampled, standard on-policy RLVR rarely recovers it. Motivated by this observation, we propose TAR, a Targeted Adaptive Replay framework that preserves diverse correct reasoning behaviors already present in the base policy. TAR constructs a compact memory bank of diverse base-model solutions and selectively replays them through an adaptive mechanism that activates only when stored behaviors are being suppressed during RLVR. Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks and two Qwen2.5 model scales, TAR consistently achieves a better balance between reasoning performance and diversity preservation than existing diversity-preserving post-training methods, while substantially reducing the forgetting of correct base-model solutions. Code is available at https://github.com/wenzhilics/tar.

articles.title: GLOSS-MT: Controllable Low-Resource Machine Translation with an Editable Dictionary
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.24730v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Adapting a pretrained machine translation (MT) model to new terminology usually requires new parallel data and another round of fine-tuning, which is costly for low-resource languages. We ask whether controllability can be added to MT, and the fine-tuning burden reduced, without degrading the pretrained model. GLOSS-MT looks up the source's noun phrases in an offline English-Twi dictionary, replaces every phrase found by its Twi translation in place, and fine-tunes a translation model once to translate these mixed inputs. We apply the same data and pipeline to NLLB-200 (600M, 1.3B, 3.3B), OPUS-MT en-tw and TranslateGemma 4B. On a document-level English-to-Asante Twi benchmark (84 documents, four domains), every fine-tune scores above its pretrained base in chrF2 (+2.85 to +5.48), and the three NLLB fine-tunes are the best open systems (50.12-50.80). A direct controllability test on human-translated Bible passages shows that the three fine-tunes tested write 79-97% of the dictionary terms, and that replacing every dictionary entry by a different term changes the output accordingly (70-97% of the new terms appear) with no retraining. We release the models, data and code.

articles.title: Who Gets Unmasked? Sampler-Induced Bias in Diffusion Language Models
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.24795v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Diffusion language models (dLLMs) generate by gradually unmasking a canvas, so their samplers decide not only which token to write but also when to commit it. We show that this second decision changes who appears in generated text, a sampler-induced bias on top of the model's own. Common commit rules, including LLaDA's default, commit the positions whose sampled tokens are most probable; this peeking favors majority options. To separate the sampler from the model, we read the model's belief about a fork, such as a protagonist's gender, in one forward pass, and show that this belief matches exact sampling from the model. Measured against it, peeking samplers on LLaDA and Dream amplify occupational gender stereotypes and collapse opinion distributions, and confidence-based ordering shifts gender-balanced occupations toward men, more so under faster parallel decoding. We propose Fork-First Sampling, which decides the fork before anything else is written: it follows the belief or any target distribution, improves fluency, and avoids the stories that remark on the protagonist's gender, which prompt-based fixes produce, at the cost of one forward pass. Fairness evaluations of dLLMs should report the commit rule.

articles.title: DiffuPlan: Editable Planning State for Diffusion Language Model Agents
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.24717v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Diffusion language models (dLLMs) are emerging as an alternative to autoregressive (AR) language models, yet dLLM agents largely inherit an interaction protocol designed for AR generation: once intermediate state is written, later observations can only be incorporated by appending more text. This is a poor match to a defining capability of dLLMs -- reconstructing earlier text conditioned on context that appears both before and after it. We ask whether this capability can support a different agent-state paradigm in which intermediate planning state is directly revisable as evidence arrives. We introduce DiffuPlan, a diffusion search agent that maintains a single editable planning state and reconstructs only the affected steps when later evidence resolves an entity or changes the search route. To support variable-length revisions, we introduce Expansion-Partition Marginalization (EPM), which marginalizes over equivalent expansion paths. We further adapt diffusion trajectory RL to multi-turn search. Across four multi-hop QA benchmarks, DiffuPlan achieves 50.24 average F1, outperforming strong AR search agents. More importantly, under identical data and training, editable planning state improves the diffusion agent by 2.44 F1 versus only 0.47 for its AR source model. These results show that dLLMs need not imitate append-only AR agents: revising committed state is a distinct agentic advantage.

articles.title: Table Serialization Determines Which Relations Language Models Preserve
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.24798v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: We study how text serialization affects table lookup in instruction-tuned language models. Our diagnostic asks the model to find the row containing a specified value under one named column, then return the value under another named column in that same row. We render the same synthetic 256-cell tables in row-major form and in column-major form with each header placed beside its values, while varying the table aspect ratio across five shapes. Across three models, the better format changes with table shape: row-major performs better on tall tables, whereas column-major performs better on wide tables. At 64 x 4, row-major leads by 42.3-54.0 percentage points; at 4 x 64, column-major leads by 35.0-59.0 points. Mapping wrong answers back to their source cells reveals a complementary error pattern: row-major tends to preserve the correct row but lose the target column, while column-major tends to preserve the correct column but lose the row. We use the term relational locality to describe this pattern: serialization keeps one relation locally available while making the other depend on positional alignment. A separate non-tabular ordering experiment supports this interpretation. Thus, apparent width-related failures in text-serialized tables depend on linearization, not table shape alone.

articles.title: Nebius Joins the PyTorch Foundation as a Platinum Member
articles.text:
The PyTorch Foundation, the vendor-neutral home for the open source intelligence layer, is announcing today that Nebius has joined as a Platinum member.
Nebius, the AI cloud company, is building the full-stack platform for developers and companies to take charge of their AI future – from data and model training to production deployment. Founded on deep in-house technological expertise and operating at scale with a rapidly expanding global footprint, Nebius serves startups and enterprises building AI products, agents and services worldwide. Nebius is listed on Nasdaq (NASDAQ: NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam.
Startups and enterprises are using PyTorch to train and fine-tune models at scale on Nebius AI Cloud. Nebius has also long supported vLLM with compute for development, testing, and benchmarking, including multi-node work on large models such as DeepSeek R1. Nebius’s Applied AI team contributes inference and post-training optimizations to open-source projects, and its open-source work has been incorporated into the PyTorch Ecosystem. As a Platinum member, Nebius plans to contribute to PyTorch and vLLM performance on the latest hardware platforms and share what it learns from running inference and post-training at production scale.
“At Nebius, we believe the future of AI depends on a strong, connected ecosystem, from training to deployment. Joining the PyTorch Foundation as a Platinum member allows us to collaborate more deeply with the community and contribute our expertise in high-performance infrastructure and applied AI. Together, we can help developers and enterprises move more easily from experimentation to production and scale their AI applications,” said Ryan Hanrui Wang, Senior Vice President, Applied AI, Nebius
We are excited to welcome Nebius to the PyTorch Foundation as a Platinum Member,” said Mark Collier, Executive Director of the PyTorch Foundation. “The strength of our ecosystem is how we work together to tackle AI’s toughest scaling challenges. By participating directly in our open source community, Nebius is leveraging and advancing PyTorch Foundation projects like vLLM and PyTorch to drive both high-throughput inference performance and large-scale model training.”
As a platinum member, Nebius is granted one seat to the PyTorch Foundation Governing Board. The Board sets policy through our bylaws, mission and vision statements, describing the overarching scope of foundation initiatives, technical vision, and direction.
We’re happy to welcome Ryan Hanrui Wang, Senior Vice President, Applied AI, Nebius, to our board. Ryan Hanrui Wang is SVP, Applied AI at Nebius, where he leads inference, post-training, and agentic systems. He previously co-founded and served as CEO of Eigen AI, acquired by Nebius in 2026. Ryan holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science from MIT, where he created the SpAtten sparse-attention framework and Hardware-Aware Transformers; his open-source work has passed one million downloads and is part of the PyTorch Ecosystem. He is an MIT Technology Review Innovator Under 35. Ryan will also serve as Nebius’ representative on the Technical Advisory Council (TAC).
To learn more about how your organization can join the PyTorch Foundation, visit our website.
About PyTorch Foundation
The PyTorch Foundation is the vendor-neutral home for the open source intelligence layer developers use for training, optimizing, serving, and running models on any chip in any cloud for any agent. As a community-driven hub hosted by the Linux Foundation, the PyTorch Foundation supports the core PyTorch framework alongside a growing portfolio of innovative projects including vLLM, DeepSpeed, Ray, Helion, and Safetensors. Through open governance, strategic support, and a global contributor community, the PyTorch Foundation empowers developers, researchers, and enterprises to build and deploy AI at scale. Learn more at https://pytorch.org/foundation
About Nebius
Nebius, the AI cloud company, is building the full-stack platform for developers and companies to take charge of their AI future — from data and model training to production deployment. Founded on deep in-house technological expertise and operating at scale with a rapidly expanding global footprint, Nebius serves startups and enterprises building AI products, agents, and services worldwide.Nebius is listed on Nasdaq (Nasdaq: NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam. For more information please visit nebius.com

articles.title: Preservation and loss of algorithmic structure in experimental diffusion of joint-action norms
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.24150v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Everyday norms of social interaction - e.g. norms of sharing space, taking turns, or queuing - are essential to large societies, offering structured procedures for common interactions. However, it remains unclear how the underlying algorithms of these implicit joint plans evolve as they diffuse through populations. Here we show that this process of diffusion can select against complex algorithms in the earliest stages. We conducted a large-scale study of experimental diffusion of novel social norms among human participants, leveraging advances in program synthesis to characterize the procedures people developed in independent populations. Inherited procedures became structurally simplified and lost during interactions between participants who inherited different variants of joint-action norms; however, opportunities for interactive repair offset this pressure, preserving complex algorithms despite misalignment. These results demonstrate that interactive reasoning mediates selective pressures on structural complexity during cultural evolution of procedural norms.

articles.title: OR-License: Evaluating LLM Agents as Real-World Operations Research Practitioners
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.24087v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Can large language model (LLM) agents deliver expert-level operations research (OR) solutions directly from original client materials, without prior expert reformulation? Existing OR benchmarks typically begin with self-contained descriptions or predefined optimization tasks, underrepresenting the translation of original business materials into professionally validated solutions. We introduce OR-License, an end-to-end benchmark of 31 instances across 10 industrial scenarios from paid OR engagements totaling USD 3.68 million. It preserves original requirements, input data, deliverable formats, and information boundaries after de-identification. To study information acquisition, we introduce ORSim, a controlled client simulator that discloses business facts without supplying OR expertise. Hidden evaluation checks feasibility and compares objective quality against original expert solutions accepted by clients before benchmark construction. Deployment-Adjusted Quality (DAQ) averages expert-relative quality across instances, assigning zero to infeasible deliveries. Across 11 frontier LLMs using coding-agent harnesses, several exceed the expert reference in conditional objective quality, but none matches its DAQ; the strongest primary Claude Code configuration achieves 88.39% strict feasibility and a DAQ of 0.87 against the expert reference of 1. Client information acquisition extends beyond clarification into solution development and validation, with some later stages showing higher confirmed issue-resolution proportions. Trajectory analysis identifies formulation and implementation failures, while task-equalized research-chain completion rates range from 24% to 45% across models on evaluable tasks. These findings motivate sustained information-gap resolution, faithful problem formulation, and evidence-linked self-improvement for reliable long-horizon agents.

articles.title: Prosodic Structure as a Critical Component in Phonemic Language Modelling at BabyLM Scale
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.24172v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Human children learn language from continuous, prosodically structured speech long before they can read, yet almost all language models train on orthographic text. Building on previous phonemic BabyLM training (Goriely et al., 2024; arXiv:2410.22906), we ask whether supplying an estimate of the prosody infants exploit improves phonemic language modelling at BabyLM scale. We compare an orthographic baseline to three conditions forming a ladder of phonological richness. All conditions are trained as BERT MLMs at 10M and 100M words. Addressing the ecological validity of existing metrics in the small-data regime, we build a lexical decision task and two semantic organisation tasks. Our new lexical decision task offers improved insights into the distinction between wordlikeness, token familiarity, and lexicality as factors. Triphone phonotactic control and pseudo-log-likelihood scoring shows that these scores reflect phonotactic familiarity rather than wordhood: every model sits near or below chance on an adversarial inverted condition, revealing prior results of this kind as partly artefactual. On our new semantic tasks, a prosodically annotated phoneme stream gives the strongest taxonomic organisation at both the 10M and 100M word scales. Phonemic models with boundary structure are competitive with the orthographic baseline. These findings suggest that prosodic structure is a key component of phonemic language modelling in the small-data regime most analogous to infant learning.

articles.title: Meta tries to scapegoat staff who downloaded torrents to spare execs
articles.text:
In copyright lawsuits over AI training, Meta has spent weeks blaming staff for downloading torrents. The company has now been ordered to name executives who authorized decisions to pirate books from shadow libraries like Anna’s Archive and LibGen, TorrentFreak reported.
In a discovery order impacting a class action raised by book authors—including Richard Kadrey and Sarah Silverman—as well as a lawsuit from publisher Entrepreneur Media, Magistrate Judge Thomas Hixon largely agreed that Meta must clearly identify key decision-makers. Following testimony from Meta staff who downloaded torrents, the order could expose a wider range of supervisors, managers, and executives whom staffers said greenlit the piracy.
Meta had been hoping to avoid detailing the chain of command, particularly for leadership involved in early AI training. According to a Meta court filing, its initial efforts to compile massive AI datasets were managed through an “informal approach" where supposedly nobody with authority made any decisions. Instead, Meta insisted that a “decision” was “made only in the sense” that some staffers “technically” downloaded torrents.

articles.title: AI短剧里的“彩票工厂”不再赚钱
articles.text:
（本文作者为 指北Focus，钛媒体经授权发布）
文 | 指北Focus
“各大AI漫剧公司即将面临裁员风暴。”
这是一句常见的当下制造行业焦虑的言论
说这句话的所谓的行业从业者因为就在几个月前，他还是AI漫剧行业最有名的幸运儿之一。
中专毕业，做过服务员、贴膜、传菜生、送外卖、房地产推销，这样的经历对他来说，没有积累。
当他做AI短剧和漫剧时，他的相关言论却能被各种引用或者转载，看来还是AI短剧和漫剧对他太友好了。
这让“只认钱，就换行业”的他有了一些所谓的“观点输出了”。
他的观点之所以能被“议论”还是因为他赚到过“钱”，做真人短剧时，他曾用15万元成本的作品，一个月赚回700万元。
2025年，他又赶上了AI漫剧。
《经济观察报》报道，黄浩南尝试制作的第一部AI漫剧就火了，毛利率一度达到70%。
这其实就像买彩票，他只是一个中奖者。
当他送外卖、做房地产推销的时候，似乎没人关心他的行业判断，更不会有人把他的价值观当成新闻。直到他在AI短剧行业刮中了彩票。
但当一个中了彩票的人，决定开一家彩票工厂，雇1200个人一起买彩票时，商业逻辑就变了。
2025年下半年，他创办的酱油文化从几十人迅速扩张到1200多人。数十个小工作室并行生产，普通员工经过两三天培训，就能进入AI漫剧制作流程。
2026年1月，酱油文化单月生产约100部AI短剧。黄浩南甚至计划，将月产量进一步提高到1000部。
但彩票工厂很快遇到了麻烦。
据《第一财经》报道，酱油文化约150部作品尚未上线，对应制作成本约1200万元。
原本预计2026年营收10亿元、净利润2亿元，后来两项预期都被下调了一半。
公司员工也从高峰期的1200多人缩减到600多人。
黄浩南的行业观点也开始发生变化：
3月，他在朋友圈感叹，AI原本应该提升效率，但接触到的人却都很焦虑。
4月，他预言行业即将出现裁员风暴。
5月，他又发了一条朋友圈：
“好消息：爆款率90%！坏消息：亏钱。”
到了9月，接受《中国企业家》采访时，他开始批评平台把制作公司当成“耗材”，吸引大量企业入场，最后只有少数能够赚钱。
当彩票好中的时候，他讲的是如何中奖的经验，当彩票不好中了，他开始讲彩票市场的问题。
当所有人都开始“刮彩票”
当越来越多的人开始买彩票，连曾经的中奖者，也可能赚不到钱了。
但这不意味着AI短剧不赚钱了，而是靠增加产量、押注爆款的方式，开始失灵了。
他们高估了一件事：只会生产短剧，还能值多少钱？
2025年，AI漫剧供给不足，谁做得多，谁就可能赚得多，雇1200个人生产，确实可能比十几个人打磨更赚钱。
然而，但AI恰恰让原本稀缺的纯制作能力，越来越不值钱。
2026年2月，Seedance 2.0发布。AI让过去需要一个团队完成的短剧，三五个人、几天时间就有机会做出来。
于是，“彩票工厂”开始不盈利了。
这些“彩票工厂”只关心每月生产多少部剧，剧本容易变成模板，人物反复使用，情节互相照搬。
过去，粗制滥造可能只是一部剧的问题，现在，AI让粗制滥造也有了规模化生产的可能。
侵权、抄袭、低俗擦边等问题，也可能被一起放大。
当然，规模化不等于违规。但光靠低成本反复碰运气，不只可能赚不到钱，还可能让整个行业付出代价。
过去，1200个人同时刮彩票，是酱油文化的优势，现在，这些反而是沉重的成本。
酱油文化这种模式不只是有“自找的麻烦，”而是这种赚钱方式，正在让整个行业付出代价。
投机式“彩票”，在规则之外
《风骚律师》里，查克形容弟弟吉米拿到律师资格，就像一只拿着机关枪的黑猩猩。
这话很刻薄，但它讲了一个道理：工具变强，不代表人的判断也变强。
AI升级了他们的生产力，却没有升级他们的商业价值观。
AI短剧行业也是如此。
AI升级了他们的生产力，却没有升级他们的商业价值观。
技术降低了生产的门槛，却不能顺便降低赚钱的底线。
这时候，内容平台就不能只关心货架上有多少部短剧，还得考虑哪些东西根本不应该摆上货架。
4月7日，红果启动低质漫剧专项治理。
截至4月15日，累计拦截、处罚下架违规低质漫剧3522部。
5月，平台拦截、下架违规漫剧20941部。6月、7月、8月，分别为14357部、12347部、8689部。
其中大部分在审核阶段就被拦截，没有真正上线。
治理也越来越具体。
除了侵权、抄袭、低俗内容，让儿童扮演腹黑总裁、演绎不适当伤害情节等，也成为重点整治对象。
反复违规、整改不力的出品方，还可能被限制上传权限。
当然，不能因此认定酱油文化那些尚未上线的作品就是违规内容，更不能把它的经营困境直接归因于平台治理。
就像酱油文化此前出品的《穿越兽世成女配，兽人弟弟狠狠宠》，也会因为内容涉嫌性、暴力、血腥而被下架。
AI让更多内容快速制作，但另一面是平台的审核和治理也需要随之跟进、收紧。
2026年9月，《微短剧发展管理办法》正式施行，进一步明确了内容审核、AI生成内容标识等要求。
从监管到平台，行业开始给过去野蛮生长的生意立规矩。
但如果治理只是把不合规的作品下架，事情也只做了一半。
不是不让你们赚钱，但必须适可而止，在规则范围内用好的内容去赚钱。
红果一方面通过审核、巡查和处罚拦截违规内容，另一方面通过精品扶持、内容推荐和创作者服务机制，为优质作品创造机会。
道理很简单。
一家公司花钱购买版权、打磨剧本、投入制作，另一家公司直接复制人物、套用剧情，甚至靠违规内容吸引流量。
如果后者可以用更低的成本，和前者争夺同样的观众，那认真做生意的人反而吃亏了。
行业规范化不是让大家赚不到钱，而是不能让不符合规定的内容成为一种赚钱优势。
彩票不好中了，不代表这个市场就没有钱赚了。
不开“彩票工厂”，还有人赚钱
黄浩南送过外卖。
四川巴中有一对95后夫妻，也送过外卖。
前面我们说过，黄浩南做过服务员、贴膜、传菜生、送外卖、房地产推销。
这些经历对他来说，没有形成多少可以直接带进AI漫剧行业的专业积累。
但这对夫妻的经历，恰好提供了另一种答案。
他们原本做广告，懂设计、懂画面、懂剪辑，最困难的时候，也送过外卖和快递。
做广告的人可以去送外卖，但送外卖不会让他过去积累的本事归零。
当AI漫剧的机会出现，他们积累的审美、设计和制作能力，让他们有了新的可能。
他们不是找一次赚钱的机会，则是带着过去积累的本事，找到了赚钱方式。
黄浩南第一部AI漫剧就火了，这对夫妻却连续失败了两次。
2026年5月，他们最开始制作《花轿抬错后》《狐狸山神》，但没什么水花。
第三次，他们从平台版权库申请了《发配边关，罪妻开荒养出战神》的IP，在卧室的两张书桌前继续创作。
6月，第一季上线，登上红果爆剧榜榜首。夫妻俩吃了顿烧烤庆祝，又回去继续做剧。
后来，这部系列短剧更新了八季，抖音播放量突破41亿。
他们没有因为一部剧火了，就急着复制一百部，而是围绕同一个IP持续经营。
同样是高产，“彩票工厂”追求的是多次中奖的机会率，他们追求的是把已经做成的事情做得更好。
而且更多的小工作室反而在持续证明，没有流程化的工厂，也可以依靠审美、版权授权和持续投入，来获得市场认可。
还比如做出最火漫剧《万妖图录传》的光宇，最初他们只是一家仅6人的小工作室。
而这样的小工作室创造了红果最大的漫剧IP之一。
这样的例子还有不少。
这些例子还在证明，短漫剧创作者、短漫剧格局，甚至是短漫剧生态都还没有定型。从平台，到创作者，再到观众，大家都在和行业一起探索和进步。
对内容平台来说，越是在低质AI内容泛滥的时期，越是依赖好内容和好的创作者。毕竟AI内容这块，还有无限可能，不只是短剧，AI长剧、AI电影，都指日可待。
只是目前这个阶段，恰好处于内容治理的关键时刻。这个治理逻辑不是不让大家赚钱，而是不能让不守规矩的内容成为赚钱优势。
一个人可以靠运气发财，甚至拿中奖的钱开一家1200人的“彩票工厂”。
中奖是运气给他的奖励，不代表他掌握了制造运气的方法。
毕竟，彩票可以批量生产，运气不能批发。

articles.title: From KTIR to SpyreCode: An MLIR Dataflow Backend for IBM Spyre
articles.text:
TL;DR
Torch-spyre’s Inductor decides how each kernel’s work is divided across Spyre’s cores and manages tensor residency between on-chip scratchpad and off-chip memory, and the backend compiler turns those decisions into something the hardware can actually run. The contract between them is represented using KTIR (Kernel Tile IR), an MLIR representation built on a data-parallel view of the accelerator, in which every compute tile can see every memory and a single logical tensor can live spread across several cores’ scratchpads. A new open-source Dataflow Scheduler consumes KTIR and turns each tile’s work into a dataflow pipeline: it splits the kernel into programs, starts from a simple load → compute → store pipeline, routes every transfer through the memory hierarchy given in an architecture description, and expands that pipeline into a nested, double-buffered, multi-instance schedule. The output of the scheduler is represented using DataflowIR, an MLIR intermediate representation that Spyre’s device-specific stages use to produce SpyreCode, a symbolic SpyreBinary plus a job plan that the Spyre runtime prepares once and launches many times, filling in tensor addresses and shapes at launch.
This post is the middle chapter of three. Extending Inductor for the IBM Spyre Accelerator described how torch-spyre’s Inductor extensions settle layout, tiling, work division and scratchpad placement, and Building Spyre as a Native PyTorch Device described how the runtime launches a compiled artifact whose symbolic values are only filled in at the last moment. This post covers how the decisions Inductor makes actually become a program the runtime can launch.
Where the backend compiler sits in the Spyre software stack
Three ideas run through the design.
The frontend decides the parallel decomposition, and the backend makes it run. KTIR is designed to carry the mapping Inductor has already chosen (which core computes what, over which data, out of which memory) so that the backend never has to rediscover it. The backend’s job is dataflow scheduling inside that mapping.
Scheduling means building a pipeline. Spyre is a dataflow machine with decoupled access and execution, so loads, stores and compute run on separate engines communicating via FIFOs. The scheduler starts from the simplest legal pipeline and refines it one transformation at a time, and every one of those steps is a readable MLIR rewrite.
The boundary is an IR, not a library call. KTIR, the scheduler’s ScheduleIR and DataflowIR are all ordinary MLIR built on upstream dialects (linalg, scf, arith, memref, tensor), and the scheduler and its dialects are open source under Apache-2.0. Device-specific lowering stages for code generation start at the DataflowIR boundary.
KTIR: the contract between Inductor and the backend
Why a new interface
One of the key requirements for efficient backend scheduling is a contract between torch-spyre’s Inductor and the backend compiler with the capability and flexibility to capture the complete data-parallel view of the accelerator, in which every compute tile can see every memory and a single logical tensor can live spread across several cores’ scratchpads.
KTIR (RFC 0682, implemented in torch-spyre/ktir-mlir-frontend) is a tile-based, block-structured IR built on open-source MLIR. Our goal was to make it expressive enough to capture data-parallel mappings from two quite different sources: Inductor on one side, and hand-written Spyre kernels in languages like Triton or Helion on the other.
A data-parallel abstraction of the accelerator
KTIR is written against a deliberately simple picture of the hardware: a set of cores, each with a compute engine and its own on-chip scratchpad, joined by an on-chip interconnect that also reaches one or more off-chip memories. The property that matters most is that every compute tile has a global view of every memory, which means its own scratchpad, every other core’s scratchpad, and device memory.
Hardware abstraction of a multi-core accelerator embodied in KTIR (from RFC 0682)
That picture matches Spyre’s shape closely: 32 cores on a ring, each with 2 MB of scratchpad, backed by off-chip device memory. Data moves between device memory and the scratchpads in sticks, fixed 128-byte chunks that hold 64 fp16 values. Intentionally, the picture leaves out details such as FIFOs, load/store units and decoupled execution engines. KTIR describes what each compute tile does and where its data lives, not how that data gets there, because working out how it gets there is exactly the scheduler’s job.
KTIR is also compositional. Arithmetic, reductions and control flow come straight from upstream MLIR dialects (arith, math, linalg, scf, tensor, memref), and a dedicated dialect, ktdp, adds the two things those dialects can’t express: explicit memories and explicit accesses. A second, much smaller dialect, spyreop, covers Spyre’s own intrinsics. The core ktdp operations are:
ktdp op
What it expresses
get_compute_tile_id
Which compute tile this is; 1-D or multi-dimensional, over the grid attribute on the kernel
construct_memory_view
Interpret a region at some (possibly symbolic) address in a named memory space as a strided tensor; no allocation, no data movement
construct_distributed_memory_view
Compose several memory views, each covering part of a global coordinate space, into one logical tensor
construct_access_tile
A structured set of coordinates into a view: an integer set for the domain and an affine map for the traversal order, so tiles can be rectangular, strided, skewed or triangular
construct_indirect_access_tile
The same, with some dimensions indexed through another tensor, e.g. paged KV-cache gathers
load / store
The only data movement: consume an access tile and produce or write a data tile
inter_tile_produce / inter_tile_reduce
Communication between compute tiles, e.g. an all-reduce of partial sums
Here is a complete kernel, an elementwise add over 96×64 fp16 tensors divided among 32 compute tiles of three rows each.
#tile = affine_set<(d0, d1) : (d0 >= 0, -d0 + 2 >= 0, d1 >= 0, -d1 + 63 >= 0)>   // 3x64
#full = affine_set<(d0, d1) : (d0 >= 0, -d0 + 95 >= 0, d1 >= 0, -d1 + 63 >= 0)>
#id   = affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d0, d1)>
// The tensors' start addresses arrive as arguments: PyTorch's allocator owns them.
func.func @add(%A: index, %B: index, %C: index) attributes {grid = [32]} {
%c0   = arith.constant 0 : index
%c3   = arith.constant 3 : index
%id   = ktdp.get_compute_tile_id : index
%row0 = arith.muli %id, %c3 : index                 // this tile's 3-row slab
%A_view = ktdp.construct_memory_view %A, sizes: [96, 64], strides: [64, 1] {
coordinate_set = #full, memory_space = #ktdp.memory_space<global>
} : memref<96x64xf16>
// ... %B_view and %C_view alike
%A_t = ktdp.construct_access_tile %A_view[%row0, %c0] {
access_tile_set = #tile, access_tile_order = #id
} : memref<96x64xf16> -> !ktdp.access_tile<3x64xindex>
// ... %B_t and %C_t alike
%a = ktdp.load %A_t : !ktdp.access_tile<3x64xindex> -> tensor<3x64xf16>
%b = ktdp.load %B_t : !ktdp.access_tile<3x64xindex> -> tensor<3x64xf16>
%e = tensor.empty() : tensor<3x64xf16>
%c = linalg.add ins(%a, %b : tensor<3x64xf16>, tensor<3x64xf16>)
outs(%e : tensor<3x64xf16>) -> tensor<3x64xf16>
ktdp.store %c, %C_t : tensor<3x64xf16>, !ktdp.access_tile<3x64xindex>
return
}
The kernel keeps four concerns apart. Views say how memory should be interpreted, access tiles say which coordinates a given tile touches, loads and stores are the only operations that move data, and linalg does the arithmetic. Notice also that the work division is already settled: grid = [32], together with the arithmetic on %id, is the partitioning, and the backend is expected to honor it rather than second-guess it.
Spyre intrinsics: the spyreop dialect
Upstream arith and math cover most of the arithmetic a kernel needs, but Spyre’s compute units also offer operations that no generic dialect has a name for. A kernel that wants one of those should be able to ask for it directly, instead of hoping the backend recognizes some particular pattern of arith ops. For that, KTIR comes with a second, much smaller dialect, spyreop, which exposes Spyre intrinsics as ordinary MLIR operations. It covers elementwise and activation functions (exp, gelu, sigmoid, silu, softplus, sqrt, rsqrt, reciprocal, realdiv), the building blocks of normalization (a combined mean and mean of squares, and the normalizing and scaling halves of LayerNorm, some with fused variants), integer and address arithmetic (including idx32toaddr, which computes base + stride × index for gathers), and compare and select. The dialect also defines df16, IBM’s 16-bit DLFloat format, which splits its bits 1-6-9 between sign, exponent and mantissa rather than IEEE half precision’s 1-5-10, along with “fused” types that carry a pair of floats as a single value.
Intrinsics appear wherever any other scalar computation would, which is inside the body of a linalg.generic:
%y = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [#in, #out],
iterator_types = ["parallel", "parallel", "parallel", "parallel"]}
ins(%x : tensor<6x64x64xf16>) outs(%init : tensor<1x6x64x64xf16>) {
^bb0(%a: f16, %out: f16):
%g = spyreop.gelu %a : f16
linalg.yield %g : f16
} -> tensor<1x6x64x64xf16>
Because they are just operations in a linalg body, intrinsics fuse with the surrounding elementwise work like anything else, and the scheduler carries them through as compute until it is ready to lower them. How each intrinsic expands into the hardware’s own instruction sequence is not written in the scheduler at all: it lives in the architecture description, as one of the device patterns described later in this post.
How KTIR captures Inductor’s work mapping
The Inductor post walked through a series of decisions torch-spyre makes before any code is generated. Each of them has a direct counterpart in KTIR:
Decision in torch-spyre’s Inductor passes
How it appears in KTIR
Work division: the per-op core split, e.g. a matmul’s 16 × 2 grid
The kernel’s grid attribute, plus affine arithmetic on ktdp.get_compute_tile_id that picks each tile’s slice
Stick-granularity layout: which dimension is the stick, and the tiled order of the others
Strides of construct_memory_view, and the access_tile_order of each access tile
Coarse tiling and working-set reduction
scf.for loops around loads, compute and stores, which run the chain tile by tile
Scratchpad residency chosen by the scratchpad allocator
A memory view in #ktdp.memory_space<ct_local, ct_id = k> at the offset the allocator assigned
A tensor split across cores so each slice fits in scratchpad
construct_distributed_memory_view over per-core ct_local views
Core-to-core relayout (lx_relayout)
An access tile over one distributed view, stored into a view with a different distribution
Reduction split across cores (partial sums of one output tile)
inter_tile_produce / inter_tile_reduce
Paged tensors and gathers
construct_indirect_access_tile
Device-specific activations and normalization steps
spyreop intrinsics inside linalg.generic bodies
Tensor addresses owned by PyTorch’s allocator
Kernel arguments. They stay symbolic all the way to SpyreCode and are substituted by the runtime at launch
Tensor shapes known only at runtime, within a bound
!ktdp.runtime_arg<index, granularity = G, upperbound = U>, kept symbolic and substituted at launch in the same way
The last two rows are where this post meets the runtime post. Because KTIR allows a start address or a size to be a value rather than a constant, every layer beneath it can keep that value symbolic until the runtime is in a position to supply it.
Tensors pinned in scratchpad, distributed across cores
What most sets KTIR apart from GPU-oriented tile IRs is the way it treats on-chip memory. A tile language like Triton describes each program instance loading blocks of a tensor from global memory, computing on them, and storing the results back. How those blocks are staged through shared memory, registers and caches is left to the compiler and the hardware, and a program instance’s on-chip storage is private to it and lives only as long as it runs. In that model there is typically no way, and little need, to say that a tensor should still be sitting in a particular core’s on-chip memory when the next operation reads it, or that one program instance should read data held on-chip by another. That works well on hardware where caches and a dynamic scheduler smooth over data movement. It doesn’t fit Spyre. There is no hardware-managed cache to fall back on, and keeping a tensor on-chip from one operation to the next is one of the biggest performance levers available. On Spyre, the scratchpad isn’t a cache that a kernel happens to hit; it’s memory the compiler chooses to use, with Inductor’s scratchpad allocator deciding which buffers stay resident, at what address and on which core. KTIR therefore makes on-chip placement a first-class part of the IR rather than an implementation detail: it simply writes that decision down.
Each memory space names a physical memory: #ktdp.memory_space<global> is device memory, and #ktdp.memory_space<ct_local, ct_id = k> is the scratchpad belonging to compute tile k. A view’s coordinate_set records which part of a larger logical tensor it holds, so if you combine per-core views with construct_distributed_memory_view, you get a single tensor, indexed by global coordinates, whose storage is spread across several scratchpads.
// X[128, 1024] f16, left in scratchpad by an earlier op of the kernel:
// 32 rows on each of four cores, at the offset the scratchpad allocator chose.
#rows0 = affine_set<(d0, d1) : (d0 >= 0,      -d0 + 31 >= 0,  d1 >= 0, -d1 + 1023 >= 0)>
#rows1 = affine_set<(d0, d1) : (d0 - 32 >= 0, -d0 + 63 >= 0,  d1 >= 0, -d1 + 1023 >= 0)>
// ... #rows2, #rows3
%X0 = ktdp.construct_memory_view %lx_off, sizes: [32, 1024], strides: [1024, 1] {
coordinate_set = #rows0, memory_space = #ktdp.memory_space<ct_local, ct_id = 0>
} : memref<32x1024xf16>
%X1 = ktdp.construct_memory_view %lx_off, sizes: [32, 1024], strides: [1024, 1] {
coordinate_set = #rows1, memory_space = #ktdp.memory_space<ct_local, ct_id = 1>
} : memref<32x1024xf16>
// ... %X2, %X3
%X = ktdp.construct_distributed_memory_view (%X0, %X1, %X2, %X3
: memref<32x1024xf16>, memref<32x1024xf16>, memref<32x1024xf16>, memref<32x1024xf16>)
: memref<128x1024xf16>
// Compute tile 1 reads rows 48-79: half from its own scratchpad, half from core 2's.
#rows32 = affine_set<(d0, d1) : (d0 >= 0, -d0 + 31 >= 0, d1 >= 0, -d1 + 1023 >= 0)>
%id  = ktdp.get_compute_tile_id : index
%row = affine.apply affine_map<(d0) -> (d0 * 32 + 16)>(%id)
%t = ktdp.construct_access_tile %X[%row, %c0] {
access_tile_set = #rows32, access_tile_order = #id
} : memref<128x1024xf16> -> !ktdp.access_tile<32x1024xindex>
%x = ktdp.load %t : !ktdp.access_tile<32x1024xindex> -> tensor<32x1024xf16>
A distributed memory view: one logical tensor, pinned across four scratchpads
This one construct does quite a lot of work. First, it lets intermediate tensors stay on-chip from one operation to the next: a producer can store into a distributed ct_local view and a consumer can load from it without either of them ever mentioning device memory, which is precisely the kind of fusion without a round trip that the softmax example in the Inductor post was built around. Second, it turns a core-division mismatch into ordinary IR. When a producer and a consumer divide a tensor differently, the consumer’s access tiles just cross scratchpad boundaries, and since every compute tile can see every scratchpad, that is still nothing more than a load; the on-chip relayout that torch-spyre’s co-optimizing allocator weighs against a spill needs no special-purpose op. Third, it keeps placement binding. The runtime post argued that “placement must be explicit and binding because compiled code may depend on it,” and KTIR is where that dependency is recorded, since the memory space and coordinate se

articles.title: Modeling Discourse Profiles in Climate Misinformation Discourse
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.24489v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Prior work on climate misinformation detection typically classifies individual comments or claims using text alone. This framing overlooks a key property of online climate discourse: misinformation is often produced, reinforced, and sustained through recurring rhetorical patterns that reappear across comments and threads. Using a large-scale TikTok climate discourse dataset, we construct discourse profiles by clustering climate-related comments into recurring rhetorical patterns. We then incorporate these profiles into fine-grained climate misinformation classifiers using a late-fusion architecture. Under video-disjoint evaluation across three training seeds, discourse-profile-aware models significantly improve macro-F1 over text-only baselines for bag-of-words, TF-IDF, and MPNet representations. RoBERTa-large exhibits a positive mean improvement but substantially greater variability, and the difference is not statistically significant. Beyond classification, our results show discourse profiles shape misinformation reception and propagation. Discourse-profile-conditioned language model agents exhibit misinformation acceptance patterns aligned with profile-level misinformation prevalence in ClimateDisc, and the relationship between misinformation prevalence and engagement persistence differs across dominant discourse profiles.

articles.title: EGIP: An Evidence-Grounded Interaction Protocol for Clinical Agents
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.24539v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Interactive clinical agents acquire evidence through patient dialogue and diagnostic examinations, yet their performance also depends on how the interaction environment exposes information, available actions, and examination results. When these conditions are implicit or inconsistently controlled, final-answer accuracy can conflate diagnostic reasoning with the effects of the interaction protocol. We propose the \textbf{E}vidence-\textbf{G}rounded \textbf{I}nteraction \textbf{P}rotocol (EGIP), which enforces role-specific information boundaries, exposes diagnostic actions without revealing their results, retrieves examination results from stored clinical records, and organizes acquired evidence for final decision-making. By separating evidence acquisition from terminal prediction, EGIP enables different decision strategies to operate on the same observations. We evaluate EGIP across two clinical-agent frameworks, five datasets, and six language models. EGIP improves diagnostic accuracy over native baselines across all primary comparisons. A clinician review further shows that the proportion of automatically scored correct responses jointly judged evidence-supported rises from 10.20\% to 36.55\%. These findings support the effectiveness of EGIP as a unified interaction protocol for improving clinical-agent performance through controlled evidence access and acquisition.

articles.title: Spain-Based Startups Advance Regional Innovation With Barcelona Supercomputing Center
articles.text:
The Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC)’s AI Factory Accelerator Programme, now in full operation following a pilot initiative, gives startups access to sovereign compute, technical support and training to support innovation across industries.
Many of these companies are also members of the NVIDIA Inception program for cutting-edge startups — and as of today, access to some of the BSC AI Factory services are available through the NVIDIA Inception portal.
NVIDIA Inception complements the BSC AI Factory Accelerator Programme by providing members with training through NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute open courses, business mentoring, venture capital connections and other resources.
An upcoming extension of MareNostrum 5 — BSC’s public infrastructure serving scientific and technological innovation, powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing — will deliver supercomputing access through the BSC AI Factory and other AI Factories across Europe. BSC AI Factory is among Europe’s first AI factories and the first in Spain, and has delivered more than 800 services to private and public-sector clients since its April 2025 launch.
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
Three Inception members were recently named the BSC AI Factory Accelerator Programme’s AI Champions at the pilot initiative’s demo day:
Qatium’s water-network platform — already used by more than 250 utilities in 16 countries — is now in early production with its Neural Water Intelligence technology, powered by proprietary AI models trained on MareNostrum 5. Built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, the NVIDIA cuGraph library, the NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo framework and NVIDIA Nemotron open models, the technology helps water utilities make better operational decisions every day.
OneCareAI, a research spin-off from BSC, used NVIDIA NIM microservices to develop technology designed to identify signs of hidden atrial fibrillation — an irregular heart rhythm — in seemingly normal ECGs, helping clinicians identify patients who may be at risk of stroke before one occurs.
Avatia built a voice-first, multi-agent system that provides pharmaceutical companies with agentic coworkers that support sales representatives and give doctors transparent, curated information about medicines, ultimately helping the right treatment reach the right patient sooner. The system taps into NVIDIA NIM microservices, the NVIDIA Nemotron 3 open model family and the open source NVIDIA NeMo Curator library.
Other BSC AI Factory startups — Agrikola AI, Elna Health, Lokutor, Montevive AI, Oppy, Pack2Earth and Up2Smart — span precision agriculture, medical imaging and knowledge access, speech services, enterprise security, sales intelligence and sustainable packaging.
The cohort reflects the breadth of what advanced intelligence can now unlock: preventing strokes, detecting breast cancer subtypes before biopsy, putting medical knowledge at doctors’ fingertips faster, replacing petroleum-based plastic with biobased compostable materials, protecting crops with robots instead of chemicals and more.
Learn more about NVIDIA Inception and the BSC AI Factory Accelerator Programme.

articles.title: SLA-LENS: From Classroom Transcripts to CSLA-Informed and Evidence-Linked L2 Interaction Analytics
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.24259v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: What happens after a learner makes an error, and how does the instructor's response shape the next turn? Investigating these exchanges across classrooms requires context-sensitive annotation that is difficult to scale manually. We introduce SLA-LENS, an end-to-end LLM-assisted framework that connects classroom transcripts to structured pedagogical annotations and evidence-linked descriptive analytics. Grounded in interactionist Second Language Acquisition (SLA) theory, its annotation schema captures second language learner errors, pedagogical functions, and uptake or repair while accounting for speaker roles, conversational context, and hierarchical labels. We apply the framework to 40 authentic online L2 Spanish classroom transcripts comprising over 21,000 sentence-level instances. We evaluate proprietary and open-weight LLMs, including task-specific QLoRA adaptation, using expert-reviewed gold annotations, held-out silver data, and metrics sensitive to different types of annotation error. A deterministic reporting layer generates reproducible visualizations of participation, feedback, learner errors, uptake, and temporal interaction patterns, linked to supporting transcript evidence. By making these patterns accessible and inspectable, SLA-LENS supports systematic classroom discourse research, pedagogical reflection, and curriculum design.

articles.title: 前苹果工程师、Jackery联创做宠物健康硬件，年营收超10亿，获红杉投资｜硬氪专访
articles.text:
摘要：从自动化工具进化为能感知、判断、通知、行动的智能终端。
作者｜黄楠
编辑｜袁斯来
Petlibro的创始人伍昱某种程度上是个幸运的人。他在20多岁的时候，赶上了中国消费硬件出海的黄金时代。
他2007年加入苹果做工程师，参与过早期iPod、初代iPhone的产研工作。2012年开始创业、联合成立储能品牌Jackery，瞄准用户的用电焦虑与充电安全痛点，希望补上苹果产品没能覆盖的空白需求。2016年，伍昱加入泽宝任CEO，参与并见证了泽宝的销售额从十亿级别飙升到五十亿人民币体量。
2019年，伍昱决定再次下场，做宠物智能硬件生意。
这在当时算不上是一个热门赛道。咖啡厅和路演现场，人们谈论着TWS耳机、扫地机器人、智能摄像头，但似乎没人关心，一只独自在家的猫，今天到底喝没喝够水。
伍昱注意到了被主流忽略的场景：朋友出差，喂食器卡粮，猫饿了一天，主人却无从知晓；多宠家庭里，一只猫需要吃处方粮，却总在别的碗边混食；猫咪频繁出现在猫砂盆里，主人很难判断是习惯如此，还是身体已经出了问题。
彼时的宠物硬件市场已经跑出了头部卖家，但大部分品牌主要聚焦在猫砂盆这一大单品，还没有在海外发力；同时，有关宠物健康数据管理与服务的场景却一片空白。伍昱知道，自己找到了一个没有绝对头部、也尚未被真正定义的赛道。
他与几位喜爱宠物的年轻人创办了智能宠物品牌Petlibro。公司先后拿下红杉、深创投等头部机构融资，年营收数亿。2021年，公司第一款智能喂食器Granary系列发布。
但这并非一款简单的 “远程投喂”器。团队从产品定义开始，其研发思路和定价策略就和行业主流打法拉开差距。
Petlibro智能喂食器（图源/企业）
过去，国内多数宠物智能厂商都信奉短平快的爆款打法，依靠成熟供应链复刻功能、主打价格竞争快速抢占市场。跨境平台上大量白牌WiFi喂食器售价集中在40‑60美元不等；Petlibro初代基础版Granary首发定价为69.99美元，同系列带摄像头的旗舰版本上市价达到149.99美元，在同类产品里定位显著更高。
这个选择并不讨巧。伍昱有自己的判断：硬件容易被复刻，但宠物数据和围绕数据建立的软件系统才不可取代。
“不仅是硬件，放眼整个宠物行业，尚未诞生公认的全球龙头，中国第一是谁也没有定论，用户端对品牌的认知高度分散。我们的想法很简单：既然选择创业，就要选择一个有机会做大、也值得做大的方向。”伍昱说。
以下为硬氪与Petlibro创始人兼CEO伍昱的对谈实录，内容经编辑：
寻找没有绝对龙头的赛道
硬氪：你个人经历中和宠物硬件的交集其实并不多，为什么会选择这个赛道创业？
伍昱：一直以来，几乎每个领域都有大量问题亟待解决，但同样也有许多强大的公司在试图解决。
比如手机行业，还需要一家初创公司进去做吗？其实不太需要。产品形态做得极致，可创新空间相对有限。用户心智里已经有了第一，甚至赛道内的前五大品牌也都有了。
我们开始观察哪些赛道还有机会；自然而然地从身边调研，也看了以前熟悉的消费电子、家电。当时在深圳，大部分赛道都已经有做得不错的公司。因此，我们首先必须说服自己，做这件事的价值到底是什么？
调研中可以看到，宠物硬件赛道有其特殊性。用户端没有统一的头部品牌认知，谁是世界第一，不知道；谁是中国第一，也尚无定论。再叠加智能属性，全球范围内真正意义上的好品牌是谁？一个绝对的世界第一还没有形成。
我们的想法也很简单。既然决定了要创业，至少要把梦想想得更大一点。
硬氪：Petlibro首款智能喂食器产品推出是2021年，据你们观察，当时海外养宠用户对智能化的接受度与真实需求处在什么阶段？
伍昱：2019年前后，宠物硬件行业整体还处在单点自动化的阶段。市面上主流产品涵盖了自动喂食器、自动饮水机、自动猫砂盆等，基本功能停留在APP远程控制、定时定量、简单状态查看。大部分品牌的产品叙事，都聚焦在怎么帮用户便利养宠。
Petlibro APP远程实时监控（图源/企业）
那时候ChatGPT还没有问世，但我们已经明确了一个方向，设备不应停留在被动控制，而应具备感知、判断、通知和行动的闭环能力。这也是Petlibro后来产品迭代的底层逻辑。
事实上，海外用户对智能宠物用品的接受度会更早，比如美国市场已经有Whistle、FitBark这类宠物可穿戴，也有Petnet等智能喂食器品牌，可普遍问题是功能单点、数据孤岛、健康闭环没形成，产品只能抓住用户初期的新鲜感，很难维系长期使用习惯。因此，我们团队希望进一步探索跨设备数据联动与长期健康服务。
硬氪：猫犬的行为习惯、喂养场景、健康风险等差异显著，为什么选择聚焦到宠物健康方向？
伍昱：宠物健康是动物生命的基础，落到日常可观察、可影响的行为和数据上，吃喝拉撒睡、运动等行为，都是健康状态最直接相关的因素。比如猫泌尿系统疾病高发，需要注意饮水量、如厕次数、尿量、体重变化等关键指标；狗户外活动更多，要关注运动量、分离焦虑、进食习惯等。
虽然猫狗的生理结构存在明显差异，但我们没有划分各自条线，而是根据动物行为、场景去判别风险差异，设计不同的产品形态和交互逻辑。
硬件只是入口，健康数据和服务才是长期价值。出于这一判断，团队并未将方向锁定在主打便捷功能的产品上，而是将健康相关能力作为长期研发重点，同时做好可靠性和日常使用体验。
我们清楚知道，结构、功能很容易被复刻，但围绕宠物健康建立的全栈能力才是难以被替代的壁垒。
硬氪：Petlibro是最早在喂食器中提出真空锁鲜概念的品牌，它的设计对宠物粮保鲜很有价值，过去却极少被业界关注，这款产品定义是怎么形成的？
伍昱：团队的产品思路相对聚焦，可以看到，仅喂食器类目的SKU就做得很细，除了真空锁鲜外，还陆续推出了多宠喂食、RFID（无线射频信号）识别等。
这些方案背后是很多细碎的用户需求。比如多宠场景，海外多宠家庭渗透率很高，仅北美地区占比就超过50%。这类用户普遍面临同一个问题，即多只宠物饮食需求不同、需要分粮喂养，但传统设备无法隔离，很容易出现混吃、偷吃的情况。我身边有养宠朋友也是如此，家里三只猫有的需要吃处方粮，一旦混食，即便不会立刻产生健康问题，也达不到精细化喂养的标准。
我们采用RFID识别技术来解决。这个方案推出的时间很早，当时大模型还停留在硅谷startup实验室里，没有进入消费硬件落地阶段。RFID项圈的路线或许听起来不前沿，但它的技术足够成熟、务实能落地，应用在规模化生产的消费级产品中，解决用户问题。
硬氪： 你们的思路是先抓住普适需求做大单品，还是一开始就用多SKU去验证细分需求？
伍昱：SKU和功能的取舍，我们有一个标准，即这个功能点是不是直接关联宠物健康，长期下来是否具备高质量数据收集闭环的能力；而不是看这个需求覆盖的用户体量有多大、能不能让产品快速起量。
以猫砂盆为例，自动铲屎是所有养猫用户的普适痛点，天然具备大单品潜质。但如果把有限资源投向除味、降噪、外观等表层体验优化，产品的价值边界容易局限在减轻日常清理负担。
Petlibro智能猫砂盆（图源/企业）
因此，在做好清洁、噪声、安全和易用性等基础体验之外，我们进一步投入健康相关监测能力。
对Petlibro来说，要做健康监测，就需要让系统能区分每只猫咪的如厕数据，精准对应到个体。因此，团队花了很多精力在融合AI视觉技术、研究重量传感器上。通过AI识别，系统可以判定是哪只猫咪进入猫砂盆、记录排泄频次、大小便类型；甚至未来我们的产品里，还会进一步提供血便、虫便等异常提醒功能。
再比如多宠识别，表面看面向的是多宠家庭这一细分群体，实则对应的是精准喂养、体重监测等与健康直接相关的刚性需求，不是我们为了凑SKU硬做的功能。
反过来讲，如果一个需求用户量很大，却和健康主线无关，我们不会把资源投进去。
多SKU是结果，不是起点。在“宠物健康” 这个确定性方向的基础上，筛出必须要做的产品和功能，SKU就会在研发过程中自然长出来。哪怕一开始产品功能不那么“大众”，我们也觉得，这才是真正值得做的事。
硬氪：这套研发逻辑最早是在哪款产品上验证闭环的？
伍昱：2023年，我们发布了首款带精准称重算法的宠物饮水机。
以前的自动饮水机产品只能检测水箱剩余水量，不具备数据甄别能力，我们产品的差异是，搭载了自研识别算法后，系统能够精准区分水量变动的原因，包括宠物主动饮水、人为加水、还是设备触碰导致的误差，统计宠物每日的真实饮水量。
肾病等泌尿系统疾病是猫咪最高发的疾病之一，根源大多在于猫咪天性饮水量不足。我们身边就有真实案例，朋友的猫确诊泌尿系统问题后，医生明确要求每天固定饮水120毫升。他用Petlibro饮水机，APP里能看到直观数据。比如今天只喝了80毫升，虽然设备没办法让猫主动多喝水，但会提示用户猫咪少喝了40毫升，回家后再用其他方式补足饮水。
其实这款产品当时在公司内部争议很大。2022年，市场上几乎没有同类型的智能化、数据化的宠物饮水硬件。它的研发成本很高，核心零部件需要做重新开发，定价也达到了六七十美金；当时打开亚马逊，平台上看到的其他产品定价大多在二三十美金。因此，大家预判发售后产品的销量会非常有限。
Petlibro宠物智能饮水机（图源/企业）
但最终表现完全超出预期，上线单日销量很快破千台。这验证了，用户是愿意为可量化、可落地的宠物健康价值付费的。同时，我们也第一次明确看到，健康数据能够在单款产品上闭环，理清了软硬件生态的搭建思路。
跳出内卷，把宠物健康从焦虑变成数据
硬氪：宠物智能硬件赛道近两年明显升温，从技术路径看，哪些方向已经出现智能化趋势？行业尚未跑通完整数据闭环，阻力集中在哪些层面？
伍昱：类比自动驾驶行业，最典型就是特斯拉FSD的迭代逻辑。它会在算力更强的新硬件平台训练完整大模型，再通过模型蒸馏，把能力压缩迁移到老款硬件上。这种模型持续迭代、跨硬件兼容的能力，迭代速度甚至超出传统工程化团队的预期。
放到宠物硬件赛道，目前行业已经看到了相似的方向，但还很难完整复刻这套数据飞轮。
核心瓶颈有两点，一是家庭场景高度非结构化。光线随时变化会影响成像，家具、人、其他物体频繁遮挡，以及宠物持续运动，视角、尺度、姿态不断切换等因素，都会导致单帧信息不稳定，连续帧之间也缺乏一致性。
二是宠物生物特征采集与标注难度远高于人脸。宠物是非刚性目标，毛发、颜色、体型、品种差异极大，姿态没有统一标准，还会随年龄、修剪、胖瘦、疾病持续变化。加上宠物不配合采集，高质量标注样本稀缺，很难形成海量、标准化、可复用的数据资产。
这也是企业普遍卡在 “能识别，但不稳定” 的根本原因。目前，我们支持按周、按月进行模型更新。
硬氪：宠物健康硬件当前呈现出哪些结构性特征？
伍昱：宠物健康硬件还处在非常早期的阶段。目前用户对设备的核心期待，依旧集中在便捷喂养、简化日常养护上。现有产品大多没能搭建起清晰的逻辑，帮助用户理解日常数据背后对应的宠物健康信号。这种落差并非用户造成，而是现阶段产品能力不足引发的认知预期错配。
我觉得核心不是“用户突然被教育明白了”，也不是市场突然出现了一个显性需求，而是产品能不能把宠物健康从一个模糊焦虑，变成一个可量化、可验证、可行动的结果。
硬氪：现在行业做到哪一步了？距离真正的健康闭环还差什么？
伍昱：目前只做到了“数据采集 + 风险预警”的浅层阶段，我们现在可以监测饮水量、进食量、排泄状态，但无法做到精准归因；比如明确量化饮水量缺口对应的健康风险、行为异常对应的潜在病症，以及给出可落地的干预、养护、就医建议。
单一设备的数据价值是有限的，真正的宠物健康，是饮食、饮水、排泄、运动、情绪、陪伴的多维耦合结果，解决的是生命状态的动态管理问题。不能归因、不能指导、不能干预，就不叫健康闭环。
当前，用户在购买并使用Petlibro的产品时，我们依旧需要投入很多精力，去解释数据逻辑、指标含义。对用户来说，他们只能通过饮水、进食、如厕、活动、体重等间接行为去判断健康状态。因此，系统输出的每个指标，都不能是黑箱结论，而必须让用户理解它从哪来、意味着什么、下一步该做什么。
宠物健康数据统计（图源/企业）
比如系统给宠物健康评分是90分，这个分数必须经得起交叉校验；系统在识别到数据异常，不能只抛出一句“存在风险”，而是能够溯源、解释诱因，并且给出可落地的建议，甚至能支持用户去宠物医院做全套体检来验证这个判断。这就形成了从数据预警到医疗验证的闭环。
硬氪：北美是Petlibro的核心市场。与其他国家和地区相比，北美用户在养宠理念、健康管理意识及消费行为上有哪些差异？市场增长节奏与你们最初的趋势预判是否一致？
伍昱：底层需求没有本质差别。收入高低不会改变用户对宠物健康的底层诉求，所有养宠人的目标，都是确保安全，改善生理和心理健康，降低疾病风险，甚至延长寿命。差异更多体现在场景习惯与审美偏好上，比如北美很多家庭是独栋住宅，喂养环境不一样；不同市场对产品外观配色偏好不同等，都属于产品形态层面的微调。
真正具备产业影响的区域性差异，集中在增值服务的付费意愿和付费结构上。 目前，北美市场兽医体系、宠物保险、订阅制消费习惯更成熟，对预防性健康服务付费意愿更强；相比之下，其他市场可能更偏一次性硬件购买，但底层健康需求同样存在。
长期看，谁能打通硬件体验、数据与健康服务，谁就更有机会将一次性硬件交易转化为持续的用户关系，进而沉淀为长期产品生态。

articles.title: 触屏Mac、防水iPad 苹果月底还有一波大的？
articles.text:
苹果今年这新品发布的节奏，多少有点停不下来了。。。九月份才刚发完 iPhone 18 Pro 系列和首款折叠屏 iPhone Duo，十月中旬又整了一场 “ Welcome home ”，一口气更新了智能家居中枢 HomeView、新款 HomePod mini 和 Apple TV。
本来托尼以为今年苹果的新品差不多就这些。
结果这才过去一礼拜，苹果又官宣了一场新品活动，时间定在 10 月 28 号，主题叫 “ Pro and Tell ”，玩的是美国小学生 " show and tell " 的梗，中文文案给译成了 " 高端局，高手来 "。
不过跟传统发布会不同，这次苹果并不打算搞一场线上直播，而是邀请部分媒体和博主到洛杉矶，直接上手体验新品，剩下没被邀请的媒体，以及屏幕前的我们，就等苹果当天发新闻稿。
按照彭博社记者 Mark Gurman 最近的爆料，这次苹果准备更新的产品，主要包括全新设计的 MacBook Pro、搭载 M6 芯片的入门款 MacBook Pro 和 iMac，以及新一代 iPad mini。
其中最值得关注的，还得是那台传了不知道多少年的触屏 MacBook Pro，按照爆料，新款 MacBook Pro 会首次用上 OLED 面板，同时支持触控操作 —— 没错，Mac 终于要上触屏了！
对于用惯了 Windows 触屏本的小伙伴来说，这事听着可能没啥稀奇的，毕竟早几年前，Windows 阵营就已经有不少能直接拿手指戳的笔记本了，但放到苹果身上，意义就完全不一样了。
要知道，当年乔布斯就明确反对过给传统笔记本配备垂直触摸屏。包括苹果后来也一直坚持，Mac 就该用键盘和触控板操作，想要直接拿手指点屏幕，那是 iPad 干的活，即便后来苹果给 MacBook Pro 加过 Touch Bar，也没打算让用户直接触碰主屏幕。
结果这么多年过去，连 iPad 都已经用上桌面级芯片、能接键盘和鼠标干活了，Mac 这边反倒终于要补上触屏。
只能说，苹果也算想通了（ 这么看 iPad 哪天吃上 macOS 也不是没可能~当然，新 MacBook Pro 并不是简单地把现有屏幕换成 OLED，再往上面叠一层触控模组。
根据爆料，苹果还会针对触屏重新调整 macOS 的部分交互，比如平时你用鼠标操作时，菜单和按钮还是原来的样子；但当你直接用手指点击屏幕，部分控件就会变得更大，方便触摸。
除此之外，像双指缩放、手指滑动滚动页面这些大家在 iPad 上早就用习惯的操作，也有望出现在新款 Mac 上，这样一来，以后用 Mac 看照片、滑网页，就不一定非得在触控板上操作。
不过苹果显然也不打算一步到位，把 Mac 做成另一台 iPad，至少从现有爆料来看，触屏更多是给鼠标、键盘和触控板增加一种辅助操作方式，而不是直接把 macOS 改造成平板系统。
毕竟真要让一套用了几十年的桌面系统全面适配手指操作，恐怕也不是改几个按钮就能解决的，所以严格来说这台触控 MacBook Pro 并没有违背苹果 “ 祖训 ”，它只是在祖训边缘反复试探~
而除了触屏，这次 MacBook Pro 的外观也终于准备动刀了。从 2021 年那次大改款算起，MacBook Pro 的设计已经沿用了五年，新款据说会进一步减轻重量，机身也会变薄一些，同时把顶部那块用了好几代的刘海屏，换成挖孔设计，并引入灵动岛。
也就是说，以后 Mac 顶部的摄像头区域，可能不再只是一个占地方的缺口，还能像 iPhone 那样用来展示一些实时信息和应用状态。
至于 OLED 屏幕本身，优势也很直接，相比现有的 mini-LED 屏幕，OLED 可以做到像素级独立发光，在显示纯黑画面时不需要依赖背光分区，黑位、暗场细节和光晕控制都有先天优势。
这点对于经常拿 Mac 剪视频、修照片，或者喜欢在电脑上看电影的小伙伴来说，还是挺有吸引力的，但 OLED 的实际亮度、功耗和长期使用表现能做到什么水平，还得等真机出来再看。
看到这里，可能有差友已经准备把手里的 MacBook Pro 挂闲鱼了，不过托尼建议你先别急。
按照爆料，这批 OLED 触屏 MacBook Pro 用的还是今年三月份发布的 M5 Pro 和 M5 Max，而不是 M6 Pro、M6 Max，也就是说，新机主要卖点不在性能，而在屏幕、外观和触控体验。
与此同时，苹果还准备给现有的 14 英寸入门款 MacBook Pro，以及 24 英寸 iMac 换上最新的 M6 芯片，只不过它们预计还是常规升级，外观基本不变，顶多给 iMac 增加几种新配色。
好家伙，普通版本 Mac 用上更新的 M6，定位更高的 OLED 触屏版 Mac 反倒继续用 M5 Pro 和 M5 Max —— 从这个安排来看，苹果更像是在现有专业本之上，又单独划出了一档产品。
至于 OLED 触屏版 Mac 的价格，恐怕也不会太客气，今年三月份发布的 M5 Pro 版 14 英寸 MacBook Pro，国行起售价已经到了 17999 元，M5 Max 版本更是接近三万元起步。
如果这次 OLED 触屏版真像爆料说的那样，定位比现款还高，那价格继续往上涨，恐怕也是大概率事件，想尝鲜的小伙伴，钱包得提前做好准备了。。。
相比之下，这次另一台新品，反而更值得关注 —— 它就是两年没更新的 iPad mini。
别看现在大屏手机动不动就往七英寸靠，iPad mini 这种小尺寸平板，还是有一批相当忠实的用户，有人喜欢拿它躺床上看漫画、刷视频，有人把它当随身阅读器，也有人买来打游戏。
但现款 iPad mini 有个绕不开的问题，就是屏幕 —— 都已经卖到这个价位了，你敢信它居然还在用一块 60Hz 的 LCD 屏幕，尤其跟现在一众高刷安卓平板放在一起，确实有点不够看。
好消息是，这次苹果终于准备给 iPad mini 换上 OLED，而且按照目前的爆料，新一代 iPad mini 8 除了换屏，还会把芯片升级到 A20 Pro，并将前置摄像头从竖屏方向挪到横屏方向。
这样以后横着拿平板视频通话，摄像头位置也会更自然，不至于总像在从侧面拍人。
不过坏消息是，虽然有供应链信源确认了新 iPad mini 屏幕总成驱动是 120Hz，但是苹果可能会通过固件限制把它的刷新率锁回 60Hz，主打一个等级森严，就看它愿不愿意大方一把了。
当然，这次 iPad mini 还有一项挺有意思的变化，就是防水。据爆料，苹果给新款 iPad mini 设计了一套新的扬声器结构，通过振动机身表面来发声，减少开孔，以此改善整机的防水能力，如果消息属实，它可能成为苹果第一款支持防水的 iPad。
至于价格，按照 Gurman 的说法，新款 iPad mini 因为 OLED 和结构升级，售价可能会明显提高，他甚至估计美版起售价会从目前的 599 美元涨到接近 799 美元，涨幅确实不小。。。
这样的话，感觉 iPad mini 还是应该还是支持高刷的，不然说不过去。
说到这里，这次苹果准备端上来的新品，基本就盘得差不多了，根据目前的消息，新设备将在 10 月 28 日正式公布，并在 11 月 6 日左右正式开卖，不过具体开售节奏仍要等官方确认。
反正距离 10 月 28 日也没几天了，接下来就看苹果还能给我们留多少惊喜。

articles.title: Which Long Documents Matter? A Controlled Study of Data Selection for Context Extension
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.24469v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Natural long documents are widely used for context extension, but which selection pipelines are effective remains unclear. We conduct a controlled comparison on Qwen2.5-3B at 128K under matched 6B-token continued-training budgets. Random sampling of natural long documents (random-long) outperforms repacking at longer evaluation lengths. Within the same candidate pool, selecting documents with high LongPPL key-token density yields further gains, unlike the evaluated generic-quality and LLM-judge selectors. We introduce truncLongPPL to reduce scoring cost by computing key-token density over a truncated prefix. At 128K, scoring the first half of the reference span yields downstream performance close to full-span scoring with a measured $2.28\times$ end-to-end scoring speedup. Across three training seeds, truncLongPPL achieves the highest mean scores among evaluated pipelines, exceeding random-long by 4.54 points on validation HELMET and 3.28 on held-out RULER, with gains most consistent in retrieval. At a 256K target context, it gains 2.82 average RULER points over random-long on Qwen2.5-3B. In short/long mixed training across Qwen2.5-3B, Qwen3-8B, and OLMo~3-7B, it gains 1.47--7.31 average RULER points over random-long mixing, with seven-task short-context averages within 0.23 points of the corresponding baselines. After supervised fine-tuning (SFT), Qwen3-8B and OLMo~3-7B models trained with selected long documents outperform their random-long counterparts by 1.13--1.67 points on LongBench v2 and 0.62--1.44 points on MRCR.
